programme.desc: Adventure junkies Simon Donato and Paul "Turbo" Trebilcock try to prove that boundaries are meant to be broken as they test their limits in some of the world's toughest endurance races. Also included are three animated shorts that have aired on WGN for many years -- "Hardrock, Coco and Joe: The Three Little Dwarfs," "Suzy Snowflake" and the 1954 version of "Frosty the Snowman." WGN's Dean Richards hosts.

programme.title: Boundless
programme.desc: Adventure junkies Simon Donato and Paul "Turbo" Trebilcock try to prove that boundaries are meant to be broken as they test their limits in some of the world's toughest endurance races. Donato, who holds a doctorate in geology, is the brains of the duo and a self-proclaimed nomad. Trebilcock, a dedicated athlete with a background in running, is considered the heart of the team. Together, they participate in competitions that include a seven-day race through volcanic terrain in Iceland, a 46-mile foot race with obstacles, and a 142-mile run through Cambodian jungles. From running, biking, skiing, swimming and climbing, their love for the rush coupled with their undeniable stamina makes it a wild ride with a few cuts and bruised egos along the way. Endurance athletes Rory Bosio and Hunter McIntyre join the team beginning in Season 3.

programme.title: Let's Make a Deal
programme.desc: CBS adds to its daytime game-show lineup with an updated version of the classic TV show of the 1960s, filmed in Los Angeles. Hosted by comic/singer/actor Wayne Brady, contestants -- often dressed in a wide variety of original costumes -- will still compete for money and prizes by striking wacky deals. Jonathan Mangum is the show's announcer, and Monty Hall, arguably the best-known host of the earlier version of the show, is listed among the new show's creative consultants. The program won a Daytime Creative Arts Emmy Award for Outstanding Original Song in 2014 for "30,000 Reasons to Love Me," composed by Cat Gray and performed by Wayne Brady.

programme.desc: Adventure junkies Simon Donato and Paul "Turbo" Trebilcock try to prove that boundaries are meant to be broken as they test their limits in some of the world's toughest endurance races. Donato, who holds a doctorate in geology, is the brains of the duo and a self-proclaimed nomad. Trebilcock, a dedicated athlete with a background in running, is considered the heart of the team. Together, they participate in competitions that include a seven-day race through volcanic terrain in Iceland, a 46-mile foot race with obstacles, and a 142-mile run through Cambodian jungles. From running, biking, skiing, swimming and climbing, their love for the rush coupled with their undeniable stamina makes it a wild ride with a few cuts and bruised egos along the way. programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.

programme.title: The Price Is Right
programme.desc: "Come on down!" "The Price Is Right" -- hosted by Bob Barker until 2007 and Drew Carey thereafter -- features a wide variety of games and contests with the same basic challenge: Guess the prices of everyday (or not-quite-everyday) retail items. Four contestants, all of whom are seated in one of the wildest audiences in daytime game-show history, are called to the stage to play a preliminary pricing round. That winner joins the host on stage for one of more than 70 different pricing games. After three such games, the contestants spin a big wheel -- hoping to get as close to $1 as possible -- in the "Showcase Showdown." The two highest winners of that round advance to the final, where prizes could be cars or roomsful of furniture. A trio of models presents the prizes.
